posts.content_md:
Hi,

I recently purchased a new 20mw HeNe from meredith. I'm not sure if there is something wrong with the laser or power supply. I find that when it's been on for about a half an hour it makes a noise like an electrical buzz and the laser dims for a few seconds. It does this every few seconds afterward. I only have left it on for less than a minute while this was happening as I was scared that something might happen to the laser (or hat I may get electrocuted . Do you think that the laser or power supply may be defective? Has anyone else experienced something like this?

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md: Could also be that the current is set too low. If this is the case, then the laser is dropping out and refiring quickly in succession. Does the supply have a current adjust? If so, let the unit warm up (until it buzzes), then tweak up the current a bit. You should find that this stops the buzzing. You may even get a bit more output

posts.content_md: Could be that the laser tube is on its way south. I'd send the whole system back and have it replaced.

posts.author: vortexx
posts.content_md:
I just tried it again and after about 20 minutes it blew the fuse. I was out of the room for a couple of minutes when it happened so I'm not sure if the laser flickered this time. Because of conflicting paperwork meredith sent I may have the wrong fuses. One of the papers recomends a 3 amp 125 slow blow fuse and the other recommends a 1 amp normal blow. The fuses I bought were the 1 amp (slow and fast blow). I replaced the fuse and turned it on but this time it blew instantly. I double checked the connections and everything was OK. I may try it one last time with a slow blow fuse. 

The power supply that came with it is a Voltex model dg-36-00 output 3200v to 4000v 7mA

Thanks everyone who helped!

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
The reason I was asking is that I had purchased a power supply from Meridith, and it shorted out on me - It was a DG-28-00, and it blew 1 ampere fuses. I sent it back, and Chad says he sent me a new one - I've not seen it yet, but hopefully it arrives soon.

I spoke to the factory, and it should **not** cook 1 amp fuses. 

Perhaps they are having problems with certain components.

posts.author: vortexx
posts.content_md: I've been in touch with the Merideth guys and it seems that some of the Voltex power supplies may be defective. They had another that they tested and seems to have the same problem. They're waiting for good replacements.
